name: Soft Blue
lede: Soft Blue is a mid, slightly violet-leaning blue built from modifier grammar — 'soft' plus Blue — first turning up as a name in the 2010 xkcd survey, though the words themselves were already common in print decades before any crowd poll.

sections.title: A modifier, and an older phrase
sections.body:
Our graph files this name as a modifier compound, 'soft' plus the family word [[blue]], surveyed by xkcd in 2010 rather than drawn from any book or pigment [1]. The phrase 'soft blue' itself is much older in print: Google Books' English-language corpus shows it peaking in the 1850s and rising fastest in the 1820s, though that count covers every sense of the words, not just this color name [2]. By our own nearest-match calculation the swatch sits closest to the ISCC-NBS category 'brilliant purplish blue' — our computed match, not a 1955 dictionary filing [1].

Its real nearest look-alike is [[clear-cadet-blue]], duller than this blue, with [[cornflower]] also duller and a little further off, and [[dusty-blue]] duller and bluer still, a little past that [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this blue in 5 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, with the stricter within-painting lens counting 4 — rarer than 77 percent of the named colors we track [4]. Two of those matches are by Henri Matisse, both from the 1910s and 1920s, too small a sample for any pattern beyond one painter reaching for it twice [4].
